versions.label: Before 2022
versions.long: Assembly seats of the 1995 delimitation of the state of Jammu and Kashmir; Lok Sabha seats of the 1976 Order
sources: Numbers, names, Lok Sabha seats: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2004, Vol. III (Assembly segments)
Reservations: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2009 (7 SC)
AC shapes: DataMeet India_AC (T3); PCs merged from them with ECI's lists
notes: Jammu and Kashmir was outside the Delimitation Act 2002. Its 87 Assembly seats (Ladakh's four included) came from the state's own 1995 delimitation; its six Lok Sabha seats from the 1976 Order.

Parts of the former state administered by Pakistan or China are not divided into constituencies on either map. The source map's seats reach past the Line of Control in places and miss some ground the 2022 map covers, so they are fitted to the ground the 2022 seats cover, plus Ladakh (1,332 km² of them left out, 2,108 km² given to the neighbouring seat), and both maps cover the same places.

versions.label: 2022 map
versions.long: Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission, Orders O.N. 6(E) (14 March 2022) and O.N. 17(E) (5 May 2022)
sources: AC shapes, numbers, names: ECI's results-portal map of the 2024 J&K Assembly election (T2, via the Internet Archive)
Reservations, districts, Lok Sabha seats: shijithpk/2024_maps_supplement (T3, Unlicense), checked against ECI's names
Ladakh: the old map's Ladakh seat (DataMeet India_AC), minus the new J&K seats
notes: The Commission drew 90 Assembly seats (43 in the Jammu division, 47 in the Kashmir division; 7 SC, 9 ST) and five Lok Sabha seats of 18 Assembly seats each for the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.

Ladakh, a Union territory without an Assembly since 2019, kept its one Lok Sabha seat, which was not redrawn; it is drawn on the old Ladakh seat's ground and numbered 6 here (ECI numbers it 1 in Ladakh).

Seat numbers and names come from ECI's own map of the 2024 J&K Assembly results; reservations, districts and Lok Sabha seats from an open layer made from the official maps. The Orders' own schedules have not been located; the totals are those reported for the final Order.
Parts of the former state administered by Pakistan or China are not divided into constituencies on either map.
